memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn around the hem of the robe, with gold bells between them. The gold bells and the pomegranates are to alternate around the hem of the robe. Aaron must wear it when he ministers. The sound of the bells will be heard when he enters the Holy Place before the Lord and when he comes out, so that he will not die." - Exodus 28:33-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Gold bells alternating with woven pomegranates ringed the hem of the robe, so that Aaron could be heard entering and leaving the Holy Place. The sound mattered. It marked that he was ministering as God had commanded, approaching in the appointed way rather than casually or presumptuously.

The closing phrase is sobering: "so that he will not die." Approaching a holy God was never a small thing. Even the high priest came under strict conditions, dressed as commanded, entering as instructed. God's holiness was real, and it was not to be treated lightly.

We can lose this. Because Christ has opened the way so completely, we can slide into casualness, forgetting the sheer holiness of the God we approach. Hebrews holds both together: we come with confidence through Jesus, and we worship God acceptably with reverence and awe, for our God is a consuming fire (Heb 12:28-29). Confidence and reverence are not opposites. Come freely, because Christ has made the way. Come reverently, because of who He is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Has my approach to God become careless or presumptuous?
How can I hold both confidence in Christ and genuine reverence for God's holiness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are holy beyond my imagining, yet through Christ I may come freely. Keep me from casualness. Let me approach You with both confidence and deep reverence. Amen.
